ai.description: Oligodon cinereus (Colubridae) reaches 60 cm. It is greyish-brown with a faint, dark-edged vertebral stripe and a distinct chevron mark on the nape. The belly is white with dark lateral spots.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Oligodon cinereus* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark V-shaped marking on the nape, which is absent in most other similar Indian kukri snakes.
ai.habitat: *Oligodon cinereus* typically inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, often found in hilly regions and foothills at elevations ranging from sea level to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Oligodon cinereus* is primarily nocturnal and utilizes its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice open reptile eggs, allowing it to feed on the contents.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon cinereus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–8 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with eggs deposited in soil or decaying vegetation.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Oligodon cinereus* is found in Northeast India, primarily across the Eastern Himalayas and Assam, inhabiting elevations from sea level up to approximately 1,500 meters.
